title: FaSTCC: Fast Sparse Tensor Contractions on CPUs
problem: Sparse tensor contractions are a core computational primitive in scientific computing and machine learning, but effective optimization through loop permutation/tiling remains an open challenge. Limited understanding of data access costs and memory requirements for different loop permutations hinders optimization.
motivation: Sparse tensor operations are increasingly common in quantum chemistry, scientific simulations, and ML workloads. Current approaches lack systematic analysis of loop permutation tradeoffs, leading to suboptimal implementations.
method: FaSTCC provides first comprehensive comparative analysis of data access costs and memory requirements for loop permutations in sparse tensor contractions. Introduces novel 2D tiled contraction-index-outer scheme with tile-aware design. Uses probabilistic modeling to automatically select between dense/sparse output tile accumulators and determine optimal tile sizes. Implements hashing-based parallel execution.
key_novelty: First comprehensive analysis of loop permutation costs for sparse tensors; 2D tiled contraction-index-outer scheme with probabilistic tile size selection; hashing-based parallel implementation.
contributions: Comprehensive comparative analysis of loop permutation data costs
Tile-aware probabilistic modeling for accumulator/tile selection
Hashing-based parallel sparse tensor contraction implementation
Significant speedups on FROSTT and quantum chemistry benchmarks
